subject: Recap: Latency vs Cost trade-offs + Pricing Target ($/1M tokens)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fintechai.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Latency vs Cost trade-offs + Pricing Target ($/1M tokens)

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned on scope and constraints: 

Key takeaways from our discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time fraud scoring for interactive underwriting flows (avg prompt+response ~120 tokens).
- Expected traffic: 4M API requests / month initially, projecting 12M in 6 months (burst patterns during peak hours).
- Latency SLO: 90th p95 target ~120–200ms for end-to-end inference (including network).
- Budget guidance you mentioned on the call: target unit economics in the range of $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Could you confirm average tokens per API call (prompt + response)? We used 120 as a working number above.
2) Please confirm monthly committed budget range for year 1 and year 2 (ballpark is fine).
3) I attached a short SLO worksheet and our pricing tiers PDF — I’ll sketch two options: a lower-latency premium tier and a cost-optimized tier (batching + quantized models).

Trade-offs we recommended on the call (summary):
- Tier A (SLO-driven, streaming enabled): 2–3x higher $/1M but consistent p95 latency under 200ms; uses reserved capacity + streaming and lower batch sizes.
- Tier B (Cost-optimized): ~30–60% lower $/1M using aggressive batching, KV/prefix caching and quantized model variants; expected p95 300–600ms.

Please reply with the token confirmation and a rough budget range and I'll put together a formal MA/quote and recommended config (batch settings, streaming on/off, target quantization profile).

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers.pdf, SLO_worksheet.xlsx
From: Samir Patel <samir@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintechai.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Latency vs Cost trade-offs + Pricing Target ($/1M tokens)

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. A few clarifications: 

- Avg tokens per call: closer to 150 tokens (prompt 80 / response 70). Some endpoints (detailed dispute summaries) can go up to ~400 tokens but are <5% of traffic.
- Traffic profile: your 4M/month initial is correct. We expect 30% month-over-month growth for the first 3 months after launch, then 10–15% thereafter.
- Budget: we’re targeting $800–$1,000 per 1M tokens initially (target unit $/1M). If we can hold latency at p95 <= 200ms, we can stretch to the higher end.

We’d love to see a side-by-side MA with the assumptions you outlined (Tier A vs Tier B) and an explicit note on when reserved capacity or dedicated nodes are recommended. Also can you call out tradeoffs for streaming on vs off for our integration?

Samir
Head of Product
FintechAI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fintechai.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Latency vs Cost trade-offs + Pricing Target ($/1M tokens)

Appreciate the details, Samir — this is very helpful. I’ve put together a concise MA with assumptions and a recommended configuration. High level: 

Option 1 — SLO-first (recommended if p95 <= 200ms is must-have)
- Model: non-quantized or lightly quantized variant in our premium tier
- Serving: Reserved capacity (Dedicated), streaming enabled, batching targets small (batch window 10–20ms)
- Estimated unit cost: $1,050 / 1M tokens (baseline for 150 tokens avg)
- Notes: consistent latency, deterministic p95 performance, higher monthly commit required.

Option 2 — Cost-optimized (recommended if budget primary)
- Model: int8 quantized family, aggressive batching + prefix caching
- Serving: Shared hosted with autoscale, batching window 50–100ms, streaming optional (off by default)
- Estimated unit cost: $650 / 1M tokens (baseline for 150 tokens avg)
- Notes: lower cost but p95 variance; good for non-interactive batch flows or fallbacks.

Streaming on vs off (brief):
- Streaming ON: reduces perceived latency for early tokens and improves UX for long responses; increases resource footprint and can slightly raise $/1M due to session management. Best for interactive underwriting where user sees partial results.
- Streaming OFF: simpler throughput-optimized path, slightly lower cost when responses are short. Works well with batching.

Attached updated SLO_worksheet filled with our assumptions and a pricing pdf with tier math. Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm you’re comfortable with the 150 tokens avg assumption.
2) If p95 <= 200ms is absolute, we’ll prepare a Dedicated capacity quote and a one-week pilot plan for peak-hour traffic testing.
3) If budget drives, we’ll scope the cost-optimized plan and show tradeoffs in an A/B pilot.

Would you be available Wed or Thu for a 30-min follow-up to review the MA and pick a pilot?

Best,
Marissa
Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers.pdf, SLO_worksheet_filled.xlsx

Subject: RE: Recap: Latency vs Cost trade-offs + Pricing Target ($/1M tokens)

Looping in a quick technical note for the pilot and pricing calc we discussed: 

- Pilot config: reserve a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) for peak 95th testing; enable streaming for underwriting endpoints and keep batching window at 15ms for interactive routes.
- Cost modeling: our $/1M token estimates assume tokenization parity and include KV cache hit rates of ~25% — if FintechAI can share a sample traffic trace we can refine to within ±10%.
- Discount guidance: for a 12 month reserved commit at the volume you described, we can look at a 12–18% discount on the SLO-first option; pricing team to produce formal MA.

I’ll draft the pilot playbook and hand to Laura to own logistics.

—Marcus
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
